column1: # The ESCAPE HATCH, and nothing else. Empty is the normal state.
# Failures explained by a SUBSTITUTION are not listed here and must not be: they are DERIVED from
# `run-latest/dropped-types.tsv`, which `PortRun` writes from the manifest on every run. This port
# drops nothing, so that set is empty and every row here is a CLAIM someone has to defend.
# A row carries `frame=<ported class>` as a trailing TAB-separated field — the `unit` the correlator
# anchors the failure at, copied from `run-latest/test-failures.tsv`. Keyed on (suite, test) alone a
# row absorbs a NEW failure with a DIFFERENT cause in the same test, silently, and the sentence
# would then be about something that is not happening; anchored, the claim stops holding the moment
# the failure moves and the failure counts UNEXPECTED. `test-failures.tsv` records
# `expected#declared` against `expected#derived` so the two can never be confused, and a declared
# entry whose test starts PASSING is reported so this line can be deleted.
# `test` may be `*` to declare a whole suite.

column3: the mapping sends java.util.Map.Entry to scala.Tuple2, and Paired/Pair IMPLEMENT that interface — so the phase kept java's parent (the counted InexpressibleParent refusal, visible as a porter note on Paired) while retyping the REIFIED `o instanceof Map.Entry` and the downcast under it in Pair.equals to Tuple2, which no Pair is at run time.
